v: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”
So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.
“How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture:
“He was led like a sheep to the slaughter,
and as a lamb before the shearer is silent,
so He did not open His mouth.

In His humiliation He was deprived of justice.
Who can recount His descendants?
For His life was removed from the earth.”
“Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”
Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”
And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.
But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

paras: One day an angel from God came to a follower of Jesus named Philip and told him to go to a certain road in the desert. So Philip got up and went.

Now, while he was on that road, he met a man from a faraway country. This man had traveled a long way to worship God, and now he was heading back home in his carriage. While he was sitting in his carriage he began reading a book from one of God’s prophets.

Then God’s Spirit told Philip to go over to that carriage. So Philip ran up to it, and he could hear the man reading. Philip asked him, “Do you understand what you’re reading?” The man said, “No, I need someone to explain it to me.” So he invited Philip to come up and sit with him in the carriage.

Well, the man was reading about a person who was led away like a sheep to be killed, but the person didn't say a word as he was being killed. And the man asked Philip, “Who is the prophet talking about here?” So, starting right there, Philip began to tell him all about Jesus. And when the man heard about Jesus, he believed in Jesus.

As they were riding along the road, they came to some water. And the man got excited and said, “Look, there’s water right here! What’s stopping me from being baptized right now?” So, Philip agreed, and they both went down into the water, and Philip baptized the man as a sign that Jesus had cleansed his sins.
Then when they came up out of the water, all of a sudden God’s Spirit took Philip away, and the man never saw him again. But the man went home, so happy and full of joy.
